storyPages.contentEn: Sangolli Rayanna was born in 1798 in Sangolli village, Dharwad. From childhood he showed extraordinary bravery and could outrun horses.
storyPages.contentKn: ಸಂಗೊಳ್ಳಿ ರಾಯಣ್ಣ 1798 ರಲ್ಲಿ ಧಾರವಾಡ ಜಿಲ್ಲೆ ಸಂಗೊಳ್ಳಿಯಲ್ಲಿ ಜನಿಸಿದರು. ಅಸಾಧಾರಣ ಧೈರ್ಯಕ್ಕೆ ಹೆಸರಾಗಿದ್ದರು.

storyPages.contentEn: Rayanna served as military commander under Queen Chennamma. His guerrilla tactics confused even the best British commanders.
storyPages.contentKn: ರಾಯಣ್ಣ ರಾಣಿ ಚೆನ್ನಮ್ಮನ ಸೇನಾ ಕಮಾಂಡರ್ ಆಗಿ ಸೇವೆ ಸಲ್ಲಿಸಿದರು.

storyPages.contentEn: Even after Chennamma was imprisoned, Rayanna continued fighting. In 1831 he was captured and hanged on January 26 — a martyr who never surrendered.

storyPages.contentEn: Kittur Chennamma was born in 1778 in Kakati village, Belagavi. Trained in horse riding and sword fighting, she became queen of the Kittur Kingdom.

storyPages.contentEn: In 1824 when British tried to annex Kittur using Doctrine of Lapse, Chennamma refused. Her forces defeated the British — 33 years before the 1857 mutiny!
storyPages.contentKn: 1824 ರಲ್ಲಿ ಬ್ರಿಟಿಷ್ ಪ್ರತಿರೋಧಿಸಿ 1857 ರ 33 ವರ್ಷ ಮೊದಲೇ ಯುದ್ಧ ಗೆದ್ದರು!

storyPages.contentEn: Though imprisoned at Bailhongal Fort and dying in 1829, Chennamma's courage inspired generations. Her statue stands on Parliament Street in Delhi.

storyPages.contentEn: Tipu Sultan was born November 20, 1750 near Bengaluru. Son of Hyder Ali, he said: 'Better to live one day as a tiger than a thousand years as a sheep.'
storyPages.contentKn: ಟಿಪ್ಪು ಸುಲ್ತಾನ್ 1750 ರ ನವೆಂಬರ್ 20 ರಂದು ಬೆಂಗಳೂರು ಸಮೀಪ ಜನಿಸಿದರು.

storyPages.contentEn: The Portuguese repeatedly tried to conquer Ullal. Abbakka repelled their attacks. In one night raid she personally led soldiers into their camp forcing retreat.

storyPages.contentEn: Kengal Hanumanthaiah was born in 1908 in Kengal village. Rising from humble origins, he became second Chief Minister of Mysore State.
storyPages.contentKn: ಕೆಂಗಲ್ ಹನುಮಂತಯ್ಯ 1908 ರಲ್ಲಿ ಕೆಂಗಲ್ ಗ್ರಾಮದಲ್ಲಿ ಜನಿಸಿ ಮೈಸೂರು ರಾಜ್ಯದ ಎರಡನೇ ಮುಖ್ಯಮಂತ್ರಿಯಾದರು.

storyPages.contentEn: Hanumanthaiah's greatest achievement was building Vidhana Soudha, completed in 1956. He said: 'We should build something that makes even our conquerors envious.'
storyPages.contentKn: 1956 ರಲ್ಲಿ ಪೂರ್ಣಗೊಂಡ ವಿಧಾನಸೌಧ ಅವರ ಮಹಾನ್ ಸಾಧನೆ.

storyPages.contentEn: He worked for rural development, education and farmers' welfare. An active voice for Kannada rights until his death in 1980.

storyPages.contentEn: His 'Ooru Keri' (1975) shook Karnataka's literary world. Founder of Dalit Sangharsha Samiti, he fought for equality.

storyPages.contentEn: Siddalingaiah received the Pampa Award, Karnataka's highest literary honor. He passed away in 2021 but his poems inspire millions.

storyPages.contentEn: Kuppali Venkatappa Puttappa (Kuvempu) was born in 1904 in Kuppali, Shivamogga. Growing up in the lush Malnad forests deeply influenced his poetry and love for nature.
storyPages.contentKn: ಕುವೆಂಪು 1904 ರಲ್ಲಿ ಶಿವಮೊಗ್ಗ ಜಿಲ್ಲೆ ಕುಪ್ಪಳಿಯಲ್ಲಿ ಜನಿಸಿದರು. ಮಲೆನಾಡ ಕಾಡು ಅವರ ಕಾವ್ಯ ಪ್ರೇರಣೆ.

storyPages.contentEn: Kuvempu wrote the monumental Ramayana Darshanam receiving the Jnanpith Award — the highest literary honor in India and was the first Kannada writer to receive it.

storyPages.contentEn: Awarded 'Rastakavi' (National Poet), Kuvempu championed 'Vishwamanava' — Universal Man — transcending caste and religion. He passed away in 1994 leaving immortal literature.

storyPages.contentEn: He established schools for lower-caste children when education was a privilege of few. He believed education was the most powerful tool for social transformation.

storyPages.contentEn: Madhvacharya was born in 1238 in Pajaka near Udupi. A brilliant scholar who could recite scriptures by age five, he showed remarkable spiritual inclination from birth.

storyPages.contentEn: Madhvacharya founded Dvaita Vedanta — God and soul are eternally distinct. He established eight mutts in Udupi and the famous Krishna temple.
storyPages.contentKn: ದ್ವೈತ ವೇದಾಂತ ಸ್ಥಾಪಿಸಿ ಉಡುಪಿಯಲ್ಲಿ ಎಂಟು ಮಠ ಮತ್ತು ಕೃಷ್ಣ ಮಂದಿರ ಸ್ಥಾಪಿಸಿದರು.

storyPages.contentEn: Madhvacharya wrote over 37 works in Sanskrit. The Udupi Krishna temple remains one of India's most visited temples even after 1200 years.

storyPages.contentEn: Vishnuvardhana built the Chennakeshava Temple at Belur and Hoysaleshwara Temple at Halebidu — architectural masterpieces and finest Hoysala architecture in the world.
storyPages.contentKn: ಬೇಲೂರು ಚೆನ್ನಕೇಶವ ಮತ್ತು ಹಳೇಬೀಡು ಹೊಯ್ಸಳೇಶ್ವರ ಮಂದಿರ ನಿರ್ಮಿಸಿದರು.

storyPages.contentEn: Vishnuvardhana's temples at Belur and Halebidu are UNESCO World Heritage Sites. His patronage of art made the Hoysala era a golden age for Karnataka.

storyPages.contentEn: Onake Obavva was the wife of a soldier guarding Chitradurga Fort. While her husband was away she discovered Hyder Ali's soldiers sneaking through a small gap in the fort wall.
storyPages.contentKn: ಒನಕೆ ಒಬವ್ವ ಚಿತ್ರದುರ್ಗ ಕೋಟೆ ಕಾವಲುಗಾರನ ಪತ್ನಿ. ಗಂಡ ಇಲ್ಲದ ವೇಳೆ ಹೈದರ್ ಸೈನಿಕರು ಬಿರುಕಿನಲ್ಲಿ ನುಸುಳುತ್ತಿದ್ದದ್ದು ಗಮನಿಸಿದಳು.

storyPages.contentEn: Armed with only a wooden pestle (onake) for husking rice, Obavva single-handedly killed enemy soldiers one by one as they crawled through the gap. She protected the fort for hours alone.
storyPages.contentKn: ಕೇವಲ ಒನಕೆಯೊಂದಿಗೆ ಒಬ್ಬಳೇ ಶತ್ರು ಸೈನಿಕರನ್ನು ಬಿರುಕಿನಿಂದ ಬರುತ್ತಿದ್ದ ಒಬ್ಬೊಬ್ಬರನ್ನೂ ಕೊಂದಳು.

storyPages.contentEn: Obavva was eventually found dead after killing dozens of soldiers alone. She saved Chitradurga Fort and is worshipped as a goddess there.

storyPages.contentEn: Basavanna founded the Vachana literary movement — profound Kannada prose poems rejecting caste. He established Anubhava Mantapa, the world's first democratic forum for philosophy.

storyPages.contentEn: 'Kayakave Kailasa' (Work is Worship) transformed Karnataka society. He promoted gender equality, literacy and rejected caste hierarchy. His philosophy influences millions today.

storyPages.contentEn: Gangubai overcame poverty, being a single mother, and gender barriers. Her powerful voice in ragas like Bhimpalasi captivated audiences worldwide.

storyPages.contentEn: Gangubai received the Padma Vibhushan and Sangeet Natak Akademi Award. Performing until very old age, she passed away in 2009 at 96 leaving immortal musical legacy.

storyPages.contentEn: Ibrahim Adil Shah II ruled Vijayapura from 1580. Known as 'Jagadguru' (Teacher of the World), he was learned in music, poetry and philosophy, transcending religious boundaries.

storyPages.contentEn: Under his patronage was built the Gol Gumbaz — the mausoleum with the world's second largest dome. Its whispering gallery is a marvel where a whisper can be heard 37 meters away.

storyPages.contentEn: Ibrahim composed Kannada and Urdu poems, played music and commissioned art blending Hindu and Islamic traditions. His tolerant reign became a model of cultural harmony.

storyPages.contentEn: Kanaka Dasa was born in 1509 in Bada village near Haveri. A Haridasa saint poet, he composed devotional Kirtanas challenging caste discrimination and preaching equality before God.
storyPages.contentKn: ಕನಕದಾಸ 1509 ರಲ್ಲಿ ಹಾವೇರಿ ಸಮೀಪ ಬಾಡ ಗ್ರಾಮದಲ್ಲಿ ಜನಿಸಿ ಜಾತಿ ತಾರತಮ್ಯ ವಿರುದ್ಧ ಕೀರ್ತನೆ ರಚಿಸಿದರು.

storyPages.contentEn: When denied entry to the Udupi Krishna temple due to caste, the temple wall broke open so Lord Krishna could give him darshan. This crack is still visible and called 'Kanakana Kindi'.
storyPages.contentKn: ಜಾತಿ ಕಾರಣಕ್ಕೆ ಮಂದಿರ ಪ್ರವೇಶ ನಿರಾಕರಿಸಲ್ಪಟ್ಟಾಗ ಗೋಡೆ ಒಡೆದು ಕೃಷ್ಣ ದರ್ಶನ ನೀಡಿದನಂತೆ. ಈ 'ಕನಕನ ಕಿಂಡಿ' ಇಂದಿಗೂ ಕಾಣಿಸುತ್ತದೆ.

storyPages.contentEn: Kanaka Dasa's kirtanas are still sung across Karnataka. His life symbolizes the triumph of devotion over caste prejudice. He wrote philosophical works including Mohanatarangini.

storyPages.contentEn: Sir Mokshagundam Visvesvaraya was born September 15, 1861 in Muddenahalli, Chikkaballapur. India's most celebrated civil engineer — his birthday is celebrated as Engineers' Day.
storyPages.contentKn: ಸರ್ ವಿಶ್ವೇಶ್ವರಯ್ಯ ಸೆಪ್ಟೆಂಬರ್ 15, 1861 ರಂದು ಮುದ್ದೇನಹಳ್ಳಿಯಲ್ಲಿ ಜನಿಸಿದರು. ಅವರ ಜನ್ಮದಿನ ಭಾರತದ ಎಂಜಿನಿಯರ್ಸ್ ಡೇ.

storyPages.contentEn: As Diwan of Mysore, he built the Krishna Raja Sagara (KRS) Dam — still one of India's largest — transforming Karnataka's agriculture. He also established UVCE and the Bank of Mysore.
storyPages.contentKn: ಮೈಸೂರು ದಿವಾನರಾಗಿ KRS ಅಣೆಕಟ್ಟು ನಿರ್ಮಿಸಿ ಕರ್ನಾಟಕ ಕೃಷಿ ಕ್ರಾಂತಿ ತಂದರು.

storyPages.contentEn: Visvesvaraya received the Bharat Ratna at age 99. He lived to 101 and worked tirelessly into old age. His motto 'Work while you work, play while you play' inspired generations.

storyPages.contentEn: Siddaiah Puranapanda was a celebrated Kannada scholar and poet from Chamarajanagar. He dedicated his life to preserving classical Kannada literature.
storyPages.contentKn: ಸಿದ್ದಯ್ಯ ಪುರಾಣಪಂಡ ಚಾಮರಾಜನಗರದ ಪ್ರಸಿದ್ಧ ಕನ್ನಡ ವಿದ್ವಾಂಸ. ಶಾಸ್ತ್ರೀಯ ಕನ್ನಡ ಸಾಹಿತ್ಯ ಸಂರಕ್ಷಣೆಗೆ ಜೀವ ಮೀಸಲಿಟ್ಟರು.

storyPages.contentEn: He documented folk traditions, classical poetry and cultural heritage of the Chamarajanagar region, ensuring these treasures were not lost to future generations.

storyPages.contentEn: His works guide Kannada students and scholars to this day. He is remembered as a pillar of Kannada culture who inspired pride in linguistic heritage.

storyPages.contentEn: Field Marshal Kodandera Madappa Cariappa was born January 28, 1899 in Shanivarsante, Kodagu. He joined the British Indian Army and rose to become the most celebrated soldier from Karnataka.
storyPages.contentKn: ಫೀಲ್ಡ್ ಮಾರ್ಷಲ್ ಕಾರಿಯಪ್ಪ ಜನವರಿ 28, 1899 ರಂದು ಕೊಡಗು ಶನಿವಾರ್ಸಂತೆಯಲ್ಲಿ ಜನಿಸಿದರು.

storyPages.contentEn: On January 15, 1949, Cariappa became the first Indian Commander-in-Chief of the Indian Army — now celebrated as Army Day. He led Indian forces during the 1947 Indo-Pakistani War.
storyPages.contentKn: ಜನವರಿ 15, 1949 ರಂದು ಭಾರತೀಯ ಸೇನೆ ಮೊದಲ ಕಮಾಂಡರ್-ಇನ್-ಚೀಫ್ ಆದರು. ಈ ದಿನ ಸೇನಾ ದಿನ.

storyPages.contentEn: In 1986, Cariappa was awarded Field Marshal — the highest rank in the Indian Army. Only the second person to receive this honor, he passed away in 1993 at age 94.
storyPages.contentKn: 1986 ರಲ್ಲಿ ಭಾರತೀಯ ಸೇನೆಯ ಅತ್ಯುನ್ನತ ಶ್ರೇಣಿ ಫೀಲ್ಡ್ ಮಾರ್ಷಲ್ ನೀಡಲಾಯಿತು. 1993 ರಲ್ಲಿ 94 ವರ್ಷ ವಯಸ್ಸಿನಲ್ಲಿ ನಿಧನ.

storyPages.contentEn: Adi Shankaracharya was born in 788 CE in Kaladi, Kerala. He established the Sringeri Sharada Peetham in Chikkamagaluru district — one of India's most sacred pilgrimage centers.
storyPages.contentKn: ಆದಿ ಶಂಕರಾಚಾರ್ಯ 788 CE ನಲ್ಲಿ ಕೇರಳ ಕಾಳಡಿಯಲ್ಲಿ ಜನಿಸಿದರು. ಚಿಕ್ಕಮಗಳೂರಿನ ಶೃಂಗೇರಿ ಶಾರದಾ ಪೀಠ ಸ್ಥಾಪಿಸಿದರು.

storyPages.contentEn: Shankaracharya founded Advaita Vedanta — the individual soul and Brahman are ultimately one. He walked all of India debating scholars and unifying Hindu philosophy.

storyPages.contentEn: The Sringeri Sharada Peetham in Chikkamagaluru remains an important center of Sanskrit learning for over 1200 years. It is one of the four sacred mathas he established.

storyPages.contentEn: From Muddenahalli, Visvesvaraya became Diwan of Mysore and built world-famous dams. His journey from a village boy to Bharat Ratna inspires every Indian child.
storyPages.contentKn: ಮುದ್ದೇನಹಳ್ಳಿಯ ಮಗ ಮೈಸೂರು ದಿವಾನರಾಗಿ ವಿಶ್ವ ಪ್ರಸಿದ್ಧ ಅಣೆಕಟ್ಟು ನಿರ್ಮಿಸಿದರು.

storyPages.contentEn: The Sir M. Visvesvaraya Memorial at Muddenahalli is a heritage museum visited by thousands of school children yearly — proving great engineers can come from the smallest villages.

storyPages.contentEn: Kempe Gowda built temples, tanks and the original Bengaluru Fort. He erected four watchtowers marking city limits — still standing today — iconic symbols of Bengaluru.

storyPages.contentEn: Imprisoned multiple times for activism, Srinivasaiah died in 1932 fighting for India's freedom and workers' rights — a martyr Kolar still remembers with pride.

storyPages.contentEn: D.R. Bendre (Ambikathanayadatta) was born in 1896 in Dharwad. His verses combined folk music, mysticism and deep emotion in a unique style that made him Karnataka's most loved poet.
storyPages.contentKn: ಡಿ.ಆರ್. ಬೇಂದ್ರೆ 1896 ರಲ್ಲಿ ಧಾರವಾಡದಲ್ಲಿ ಜನಿಸಿ ಜಾನಪದ, ಆಧ್ಯಾತ್ಮ ಮತ್ತು ಭಾವ ಸಂಯೋಜಿಸಿ ಕಾವ್ಯ ರಚಿಸಿದರು.

storyPages.contentEn: Bendre received the Jnanpith Award in 1973 for 'Naaku Tanti' — only the second Kannada writer to receive India's highest literary honor. His poem 'Haluvina Haadu' is a masterpiece.
storyPages.contentKn: 1973 ರಲ್ಲಿ 'ನಾಕು ತಂತಿ' ಕೃತಿಗೆ ಜ್ಞಾನಪೀಠ ಪ್ರಶಸ್ತಿ ಪಡೆದ ಎರಡನೇ ಕನ್ನಡ ಲೇಖಕ.

storyPages.contentEn: Bendre's poems are still sung at cultural events across Karnataka. With over 30 collections, he passed away in 1981 leaving an immortal poetic legacy alive in every Kannadiga's heart.

storyPages.contentEn: Akkamahadevi was a 12th century Kannada saint poet born in Udutadi, Gadag. Devoted to Lord Shiva as 'Chenna Mallikarjuna', she renounced worldly life from childhood for her spiritual journey.
storyPages.contentKn: ಅಕ್ಕಮಹಾದೇವಿ 12ನೇ ಶತಮಾನ ಗದಗ ಉಡುತಡಿಯಲ್ಲಿ ಜನಿಸಿ ಶಿವ ಭಕ್ತಿಯಲ್ಲಿ ಲೋಕವ ತ್ಯಜಿಸಿದರು.

storyPages.contentEn: Akkamahadevi's vachanas explore divine love, liberation and rejection of social norms. She was a close disciple of Basavanna at Kalyana. Her famous vachanas begin with 'Chenna Mallikarjuna'.
storyPages.contentKn: ಅಕ್ಕಮಹಾದೇವಿ ವಚನಗಳು ದೈವಿ ಪ್ರೀತಿ ಮತ್ತು ಮುಕ್ತಿ ಅನ್ವೇಷಿಸುತ್ತವೆ. ಬಸವಣ್ಣ ಶಿಷ್ಯರಾಗಿ ಕಲ್ಯಾಣದಲ್ಲಿ ಸೇರಿದರು.

storyPages.contentEn: Akkamahadevi is one of the greatest figures in Vachana literature and a feminist icon ahead of her time. Her vachanas are taught in schools across Karnataka today.

storyPages.contentEn: Purandaradasa was born as Srinivasa Nayaka in 1484 near Bagalkot. A wealthy diamond merchant, he renounced his vast wealth after spiritual awakening and became devoted disciple of Lord Vittala.
storyPages.contentKn: ಪುರಂದರದಾಸ 1484 ರಲ್ಲಿ ಬಾಗಲಕೋಟೆ ಸಮೀಪ ಜನಿಸಿ ವ್ಯಾಪಾರಿ ಸಂಪತ್ತು ತ್ಯಜಿಸಿ ವಿಟ್ಠಲ ಭಕ್ತರಾದರು.

storyPages.contentEn: Purandaradasa composed over 475,000 songs in Kannada and Sanskrit, earning 'Father of Carnatic Music' title. He systematized Carnatic music teaching with graded lessons still used today.
storyPages.contentKn: 4,75,000 ಕ್ಕೂ ಹೆಚ್ಚು ಕೃತಿ ರಚಿಸಿ 'ಕರ್ನಾಟಕ ಸಂಗೀತ ಜನಕ' ಬಿರುದು ಪಡೆದರು.

storyPages.contentEn: Purandaradasa's devaranamas like 'Bhagyada Lakshmi Baaramma' are sung at homes across Karnataka daily. His music transcended caste and religion, making devotion accessible to all.

storyPages.contentEn: Bhima Nayak was a 19th century tribal leader from Yadgir who organized resistance against British tax collection and exploitation of tribal communities.

storyPages.contentEn: Using forest knowledge, Bhima Nayak led guerrilla resistance against British forces who tried to control tribal lands. He united several tribal communities under one banner of freedom.
storyPages.contentKn: ಅರಣ್ಯ ಜ್ಞಾನ ಬಳಸಿ ಗೆರಿಲ್ಲಾ ಪ್ರತಿರೋಧ ನಡೆಸಿ ಅನೇಕ ಬುಡಕಟ್ಟು ಜನ ಒಂದು ಮಾಡಿದರು.

storyPages.contentEn: Bhima Nayak's memory lives in tribal oral traditions and folk songs. He is a symbol of resistance and dignity for the tribal communities of Yadgir and surrounding districts.

storyPages.contentEn: Hakka (Harihara I) and Bukka were two brothers who founded the Vijayanagara Empire in 1336 CE with Hampi as capital. With saint Vidyaranya's blessings they built one of India's greatest empires.
storyPages.contentKn: ಹಕ್ಕ ಮತ್ತು ಬುಕ್ಕ 1336 CE ಹಂಪಿ ರಾಜಧಾನಿಯಾಗಿ ವಿಜಯನಗರ ಸಾಮ್ರಾಜ್ಯ ಸ್ಥಾಪಿಸಿದರು.

storyPages.contentEn: They founded the empire to protect Hindu culture from the Delhi Sultanate's expansion into South India. Under their rule arts, literature and temples of Karnataka flourished tremendously.
storyPages.contentKn: ದೆಹಲಿ ಸುಲ್ತಾನಶಾಹಿ ವಿರುದ್ಧ ಹಿಂದೂ ಸಂಸ್ಕೃತಿ ರಕ್ಷಿಸಲು ಸಾಮ್ರಾಜ್ಯ ಸ್ಥಾಪಿಸಿದರು.

storyPages.contentEn: Hakka and Bukka laid the foundation for 200 years of Vijayanagara glory. Their capital Hampi became a city of magnificent temples. Today Hampi is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
storyPages.contentKn: 200 ವರ್ಷ ವಿಜಯನಗರ ವೈಭವಕ್ಕೆ ಅಡಿಗಲ್ಲು ಹಾಕಿದರು. ಹಂಪಿ ಇಂದು UNESCO ವಿಶ್ವ ಪರಂಪರೆ ತಾಣ.

storyPages.contentEn: Davangere Veeresh was a local freedom fighter who participated in the Indian independence movement from the Davangere region. He organized local people to resist British rule through non-violent means.
storyPages.contentKn: ದಾವಣಗೆರೆ ವೀರೇಶ ದಾವಣಗೆರೆ ಪ್ರದೇಶದ ಸ್ಥಳೀಯ ಸ್ವಾತಂತ್ರ್ಯ ಹೋರಾಟಗಾರ. ಅಹಿಂಸಾ ಮಾರ್ಗದಲ್ಲಿ ಬ್ರಿಟಿಷ್ ವಿರೋಧ ಸಂಘಟಿಸಿದರು.

storyPages.contentEn: He participated in the Quit India Movement of 1942, was imprisoned for his activism and continued fighting for freedom even after release. He inspired many youths in the Davangere region to join the independence movement.
storyPages.contentKn: 1942 ರ ಭಾರತ ಬಿಟ್ಟು ತೊಲಗಿ ಚಳವಳಿಯಲ್ಲಿ ಭಾಗವಹಿಸಿ ಸೆರೆ ಸೇರಿ ದಾವಣಗೆರೆ ಯುವಕರಿಗೆ ಸ್ಫೂರ್ತಿ ನೀಡಿದರು.

storyPages.contentEn: Veeresh's legacy lives on in Davangere as a symbol of local resistance. The region remembers him through local commemorations and historical records preserved in district archives.
storyPages.contentKn: ದಾವಣಗೆರೆ ಜಿಲ್ಲೆ ಸ್ಥಳೀಯ ಪ್ರತಿರೋಧದ ಸಂಕೇತ ವೀರೇಶರ ನೆನಪು ಜಿಲ್ಲಾ ಇತಿಹಾಸ ದಾಖಲೆಗಳಲ್ಲಿ ಸಂರಕ್ಷಿತ.
